question.text: Among the following compounds, which one has the shortest <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>–</mo><mi>Cl</mi></math> bond?

solution.text: Due to conjugation of lone pair of chlorine with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi></math> bond of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, partial double bond character decrease bond length that’s why <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>CH</mi><mo>–</mo><mi>Cl</mi></math> have <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>–</mo><mi>Cl</mi></math>shortest bond length.
